Unlike prior motion retargeting methods that primarily focus on transferring human motion alone, our goal is to preserve not only the semantics of the original body movement but also consistent interaction between the character and the manipulated object, while jointly producing aligned target human and object motions. Given source HOI motion, object geometry, and contact cues extracted from the source interaction, ReCHOIR retargets an HOI sequence to target characters with different skeletal configurations while maintaining both motion semantics and contact-consistent interaction patterns. Our method builds on a Part-Aware Motion Embedding (PAME) autoencoder, which encodes full-body motion into a shared body-part-wise latent space. This representation enables generalization across heterogeneous skeletons while preserving local motion semantics beneficial for part-aware adaptation in HOI retargeting. On top of this representation, we introduce a contact-guided retargeting module and an object motion decoder for HOI retargeting. The contact-guided retargeting module treats the source object interaction as a condition for refining target character motion: object- and contact-related signals are encoded into a body-part-aligned latent representation and injected into decoding through a residual control branch, enabling stronger adaptation in interaction-relevant body regions without discarding the underlying motion prior. In parallel, the object motion decoder predicts a target object motion aligned with the refined target character motion, ensuring that the object trajectory remains consistent with how the interaction is realized by the target character. Experiments and ablation studies across diverse interaction scenarios and target characters demonstrate that ReCHOIR effectively preserves contact timing, contact locations, and overall interaction plausibility.

10.1145/3842578.title: Tele360: Real-Time Feed-forward Human Reconstruction from Sparse Unposed Cameras
10.1145/3842578.abstract: Live free-viewpoint visualization of real humans is critical for immersive communication and interactive digital experiences. Existing methods either rely on computationally expensive optimization or require calibrated cameras and low-resolution inputs, making real-time high-resolution deployment impractical. In this work, we present Tele360, the first real-time feedforward system for dynamic human reconstruction and live free-viewpoint visualization from sparse, unposed RGB streams. Our system jointly estimates camera poses and reconstructs a dynamic 3D Gaussian representation for each time instance in a single forward pass. To achieve this, we start by designing a lightweight sparsity-aware multi-view transformer backbone that tokenizes foreground human regions while preserving global context through a shared scene token. We then employ a fully transformer-based Gaussian decoder to mitigate convolution-induced over-smoothing while keeping decoding sparse and efficient. In addition, we introduce a hybrid feature pyramid that injects multi-scale appearance cues into geometry prediction. We further introduce a lightweight differentiable Levenberg-Marquardt camera refinement layer to enhance multi-view consistency and geometric alignment. Moreover, to stabilize learning under sparse, unposed inputs, we transfer multi-view geometry priors from a large visual-geometry foundation model via teacher-student distillation. Finally, the predicted Gaussian maps are streamed with video codecs to remote devices for interactive free-viewpoint rendering. Together, these designs form a balanced pipeline between efficiency and fidelity. Extensive experiments show that Tele360 achieves state-of-the-art visual quality on studio benchmarks while supporting real-time 2K input-to-rendering at over 25 FPS on a single consumer GPU. Additional captured sequences illustrate its performance across varied subjects, clothing, and motions under our multi-camera setup. Inference code and pretrained weights will be released.

10.1145/3842525.title: Gauge-Equivariant Attention for Rotation-Stable 360° Scene Understanding
10.1145/3842525.abstract: Panoramic 360° scene understanding increasingly relies on icosphere transformers, but a state-of-the-art spherical model loses more than half of its segmentation accuracy when the camera rotates by 90°, and controlled ablations identify gauge dependence in its relative-position bias as a major contributor. We propose gauge-equivariant relative position encoding (GE-RPE) : a parameter-free Reynolds average of the bias over a finite cyclic subgroup C n ⊂ SO(2) of gauge rotations. Plugged into a SphereUFormer backbone the change is invisible at deployment—zero added parameters and 1.5–4.4% forward latency—and the matched three-seed GE-RPE model records a 1.3% drop; the published SphereUFormer checkpoint records 53% under the same stress protocol but a different training recipe. Once the gauge defect is removed and a teacher-token permutation π R aligns the SSL views to the rotated student frame, iBOT+MAE pretraining stops being a liability and becomes a clean low-label lever: the full framework EquiSSL (GE-RPE + π R + iBOT+MAE) tightens the drop to 0.8% at 68.30% val mIoU and lifts 1%-label fine-tuning by +2.39 mIoU on the N =373 test split (and by +4.10 on the smaller N =40 val split); the same fix carries over to monocular depth and to zero-shot Structured3D segmentation. The construction is provably C n - invariant and O( n -2 )-close to the continuous SO(2) average, making the resulting model a usable 360° visual-computing primitive across panoramic relighting, immersive video, and cross-dataset transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/Jaywalk18/equissl-release.

10.1145/3842559.title: Dirichlet Splatting: Differentiable Rendering for Wave-Based Inverse Problems
10.1145/3842559.abstract: We present Dirichlet Splatting , a physically grounded differentiable rendering method for inverse problems with wave-based coherent sensors. Unlike optical cameras, these sensors observe a scene in a band-limited Fourier space whose continuous point response is complex-valued and oscillatory. Our key observation is that the point spread function of a reflector in this Fourier space is the Dirichlet kernel , not a Gaussian. We instantiate each splat as a Dirichlet kernel in closed form, model each primitive as a planar surfel rendered through a surfel-aware Dirichlet splat whose complex amplitude is set by wave propagation physics, and introduce a sliding Frank-Wolfe adaptation tailored to the rugged, non-convex landscape that the Dirichlet oscillation induces. On terahertz tomography, Dirichlet Splatting recovers reflector geometry with an order of magnitude fewer parameters, faster convergence, and higher accuracy than 3D Gaussian Splatting.

10.1145/3842522.title: DecomVoxel: Harnessing 3D-Native Priors with Guided In-situ Denoising Optimization for Decompositional Scene Reconstruction
10.1145/3842522.abstract: Decompositional scene reconstruction aims to reconstruct high-quality objects and background, yet existing methods still struggle with the level of quality under heavy occlusions. While generative priors offer a potential solution, 2D image-based priors often suffer from multi-view inconsistency due to a lack of 3D awareness. Conversely, 3D-native priors provide stronger structural inductive biases but frequently lead to spatial drift and misalignment within complex scenes. To address these issues, we propose DecomVoxel, formulating object completion as a guided in-situ denoising optimization that bridges 3D-native priors with neural scene reconstruction. Our framework introduces a reformulated epsilon-based distillation loss to ensure stable latent refinement, alongside adaptive spatial guidance that utilizes occupied and vacant anchors with temporal annealing to suppress generative hallucinations and mitigate spatial drift. Experiments on Replica and ScanNet++ show that DecomVoxel significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods while faithfully preserving the original spatial layout, structural fidelity, and style-consistent texture. Our method pushes the boundary of decompositional reconstruction by delivering high-quality textured meshes with clean topology, geometry, and appearance, providing a robust solution for the decompositional reconstruction of complex real-world scenes. Code is available at https://github.com/DecomVoxel/DecomVoxel.

10.1145/3842534.title: CLOTHO: Canonicalizing IMUs from Loose Inertial Garments for Accurate Human Motion Tracking
10.1145/3842534.abstract: Garment-mounted inertial measurement units (IMUs) offer a promising path toward comfortable, unobtrusive, and scalable human motion capture, yet their performance still lags behind tightly attached inertial systems. The central challenge is that loose-wear IMUs provide only indirect, garment-mediated measurements of the underlying body dynamics. The sensor-body coupling is configuration-dependent, varying with garment material, fit, sensor placement, and IMU layout, while long-term inertial drift further perturbs the observation space. Consequently, identical body motions can induce substantially different inertial measurements across garments, yielding heterogeneous, noisy, and temporally drifting observations. In this paper, we introduce CLOTHO , an IMU canonicalization framework for garment-based inertial motion capture. Rather than directly mapping loose-wear IMUs to body pose, CLOTHO reformulates garment-based motion capture as an IMU canonicalization problem: recovering clean, drift-corrected, and spatially complete tight-wear inertial signals from corrupted and incomplete loose-wear observations. To train and evaluate CLOTHO, we collect the largest garment-based inertial motion capture dataset to date, comprising 12.5M IMU frames, approximately 116 hours of recordings, and five garment designs with diverse materials, layouts, IMU counts, and sensing hardware. Extensive experiments show that a single fixed CLOTHO model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, zero-shot generalization to unseen garments, and improved robustness during long-term tracking. We also find that CLOTHO demonstrates superior scaling behavior, enabling practical deployment across diverse everyday garments. We will open-source all our code, model weights, hardware designs, and datasets to facilitate future research. Code and data for this paper are available at https://github.com/xiaoxiagao29/CLOTHO-mocap.

10.1145/3842553.title: DynaConTalk: Wavelet-Constrained Diffusion for Long-Form and Controllable Holistic Co-Speech 3D Motion
10.1145/3842553.abstract: Holistic co-speech animation is prone to averaging in both motion representation and speech conditioning. In coordinate-space diffusion, slow body posture, mid-frequency gesture strokes, and fast hand or facial details are entangled in one prediction target, often producing low-variance, over-smoothed motion. Meanwhile, fixed multimodal conditioning can let dense rhythmic and acoustic cues dominate sparse semantic cues, weakening rare content-specific gestures. We present DynaConTalk, a wavelet-constrained diffusion framework for long-form and controllable holistic co-speech motion generation. DynaConTalk performs diffusion in stationary wavelet transform (SWT) coefficient space, where temporally aligned bands separate coarse posture evolution, gesture strokes, and high-frequency expressive details. We further introduce dynamic proposal-consensus conditioning to adaptively balance rhythmic, acoustic, semantic, textual, and identity/activity cues according to the current speech context and denoising state. Finally, to ensure smooth transitions between windows and support flexible user control, we re-noise any reference signal - whether a keypose, a motion clip, or a short boundary condition - to match the current diffusion timestep before injecting it into the denoiser. This unified strategy allows seamless long-form generation, localized editing, and style-driven guidance to be handled within a single coherent process, without task-specific modules or post-hoc stitching. Experiments show that DynaConTalk improves gesture realism, facial accuracy, temporal continuity, and controllable editing over prior holistic co-speech generation methods. Code and data for this paper are at https://zhuyifeiabcd1.github.io/DynaConTalk/.

10.1145/3847303.title: Design for Machinability: Topology Optimization for Subtractive Machining Using Trimmed Neural Fields
10.1145/3847303.abstract: Topology optimization has found significant utility in additive manufacturing, but the resulting geometries are often difficult to realize using subtractive methods. The complex, curved surfaces of optimized designs typically require time-consuming point milling operations. In contrast, geometries composed of developable surfaces are well suited to flank milling, enabling substantial improvements in machining efficiency and surface quality. However, globally minimizing Gaussian curvature leads to overly simplistic designs. We address this challenge with a novel method that represents geometry using three implicit neural fields, optimized to produce machinable components. The resulting designs consist of regions of developable surfaces separated by seamlines where curvature is concentrated. Seamlines are efficiently computed as intersections of the implicit fields, while the geometry emerges through their product. By constraining surfaces to align with the cutter’s normal or tangential direction, our approach further accommodates practical constraints of 3-axis machining. We demonstrate concurrent optimization of topology and Gaussian curvature, enabling control over seamline feature scale. Compared to methods that enforce subtractive machinability without considering milling efficiency, our approach consistently reduces machining time while maintaining competitive structural performance.

10.1145/3842584.title: TempFit: Panoptic Symbol Spotting via Template Fitting
10.1145/3842584.abstract: In this paper, we introduce TempFit , a novel approach for the problem of Panoptic Symbol Spotting on CAD drawings. Existing methods treat symbol spotting as a per-primitive classification or mask-prediction task, with no explicit constraint enforcing that the primitives assigned to one instance form a spatially connected group. As a result, predictions may erroneously merge primitives from distant symbols into a single instance or fragment a coherent symbol across multiple predictions. Motivated by the professional "retrieve-and-transform" CAD design workflow, we reformulate this task as a Template Fitting problem, where each foreground instance is detected by retrieving and aligning a canonical template from a library, enforcing structural completeness by construction. Building on this formulation, we present an autoregressive transformer that unifies template retrieval and pose prediction within a single end-to-end pipeline. The framework treats the template library as an explicit geometric memory, parsing background regions in parallel via learnable background tokens and synthesizing foreground instances autoregressively while attending to template-specific geometry at each step. Experiments on FloorplanCAD and our newly collected IndustryCAD dataset, a more challenging benchmark with complex industrial symbols, heavy occlusion, and wide scale variation, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with particularly large gains on IndustryCAD. Project page: https://tempfit-project.github.io/.

10.1145/3842558.title: Efficient Open-Boundary Poisson Solves
10.1145/3842558.abstract: Poisson equations arise pervasively in computer graphics, yet efficiently solving them on unbounded domains remains a long-standing challenge. Existing approaches attempting to model boundary conditions at infinity either incur prohibitive computational costs by expanding the simulation domain, sacrifice accuracy through artificial boundary conditions, or lack the flexibility to handle varying coefficients. In this paper, we introduce a simple and practical method for solving generalized Poisson equations on finite domains with open boundaries, enabling exact enforcement of asymptotic conditions at infinity. Our method couples a finite-volume interior solver with a boundary-element formulation of the exterior problem, enforcing continuity of both the solution and its normal derivative across an artificial boundary. Inspired by Johnson-Nédélec coupling and interface relaxation, we develop a partitioned, iterative scheme based on damped fixed-point iterations, which leverages fast, inexact boundary-element solves for the exterior problem and efficient sparse solves for the interior. Theoretical analysis and empirical tests confirm that our method provides superior accuracy and performance compared to existing ad-hoc solutions across a variety of graphics applications.

10.1145/3842530.title: UniffordInteractor: Reasoning the Unified Affordance for Human and Multi-Object Interaction
10.1145/3842530.abstract: Deriving plausible and dynamic Human Object Interaction (HOI) has gained tremendous progress in Embodied AI and Immersive AR/VR. While existing HOI methods have effectively explored human interaction with individual or fixed objects, they still show limitations in complex multi-object interaction scenes. Meanwhile, previous approaches focus more on the contact information held by human-object relation, overlooking the significance of the contact situation of various entities ( i.e. , object-object). To address these limitations, we propose UniffordInteractor , a Reasoning-then-Interacting framework that leverages unified affordance for realistic and long-horizon human and multi-object interaction modeling. At the reasoning stage, we devise a Unified Affordance Reasoner (UAR) that employs a fine-tuned 3D Multimodal Large Language Model for unified object-centric affordance prediction. At the interacting stage, we propose Hierarchical Interaction Generator (HIG) , which formulates the interaction generation as a hierarchical ( e.g. , root→body→hand→objects) autoregressive prediction, conditioned on the obtained unified affordance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniffordInteractor surpasses SOTA counterparts in human and multi-object interaction generation. Our project page is available at this site. Code and dataset will be released upon publication.

10.1145/3842521.title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
10.1145/3842521.abstract: In physically based rendering (PBR) content creation, high-quality material generation remains a fundamental challenge, primarily hindered by the absence of standardized representations across existing datasets and synthesis pipelines. The heterogeneity in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterization schemes introduces significant inconsistencies, ultimately leading to unstable and physically implausible PBR synthesis results. To systematically address these limitations, we propose MIKU, a unified framework that establishes standardized PBR asset representation and enables physically consistent material generation across diverse 3D content domains. Our core contribution is a comprehensive unified PBR material processing pipeline that standardizes the entire workflow from data preprocessing to final texture synthesis. This pipeline enforces consistent representation across geometry and texture domains throughout material generation. Critically, it addresses the long-standing challenge of inconsistent material parameterizations by introducing a normalization scheme that harmonizes diverse input sources into a common representation space, enabling robust cross-dataset training and inference. Building upon this principled formulation, we train a novel physically aware diffusion model specifically designed for PBR texture generation. Our model operates within a two-stage multi-view synthesis framework. The first stage focuses on geometry-aware albedo generation, where multi-view albedo maps are synthesized under explicit geometric guidance to ensure cross-view appearance consistency. The second stage performs metallic-roughness (MR) generation using our trained diffusion model, which predicts physically plausible roughness and metallic maps conditioned on the generated albedo and the unified representation. The model is trained end-to-end on standardized data, learning to generate materials that respect category-level material priors and semantic part boundaries. By explicitly decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis, MIKU substantially improves both the stability and physical consistency of generated materials. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both texture quality and semantic consistency across different object parts, significantly advancing automated material generation for 3D content creation workflows.

10.1145/3842583.title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
10.1145/3842583.abstract: Generating physically based rendering (PBR) texture maps for a 3D mesh from a single reference image is highly ambiguous, as the observed appearance entangles material identity, surface reflectance, and illumination. While current generative methods produce realistic albedo maps, they still struggle to infer accurate metallic and roughness attributes for relighting. We present UltraTex, a cascaded multi-view framework that moves beyond appearance matching by integrating physical knowledge into multi-view diffusion-based PBR generation. UltraTex first jointly predicts albedo and world-space shading normals to generate more detailed albedo maps, and then predicts metallic-roughness (MR) maps conditioned on the generated albedo, reference image, and material semantic priors. To inject material semantics, a lightweight adapter transforms hidden-layer features of a vision-language model (VLM) into intrinsic material representation tokens, providing part-level knowledge anchors for MR estimation. To model material-light interaction, photometric representation alignment guides intermediate diffusion features toward ground-truth material renderings under controlled lighting. This makes metallic and roughness variations observable through highlight intensity, specular sharpness, and local reflectance contrast, providing stronger guidance for fine-grained material prediction without explicit lighting supervision. Extensive experiments show that UltraTex generates high-quality textures and outperforms existing open-source and commercial methods in visual fidelity, material accuracy, and physical plausibility.

10.1145/3842580.title: CSG Sweeps: Feature-aware sweep surfacing of deformable CSGs
10.1145/3842580.abstract: Computing the sweep surface of a moving 3D solid is a fundamental problem in computer graphics. The problem is particularly challenging when the solid is piecewise-smooth, which yields a complex network of sharp features on the sweep surface. Few methods can model these features, and they are all limited to rigid-body motions (translation and rotation). We present the first feature-aware method to surface the sweep of a deforming piecewise-smooth shape. Our method works on any input represented as a 4D time-varying CSG, allowing changes to both geometry and topology during sweeping. Our technical contributions include a generalization of the lifted sweeping formulation from smooth functions to CSG functions, and robust algorithms for discretizing multiple intersecting implicit surfaces in arbitrary dimensions. We demonstrate our algorithm for capturing the sharp features on the sweep surface under both rigid and non-rigid motions.

10.1145/3842562.title: Stealthy Blue Noise
10.1145/3842562.abstract: Blue noise point sets are both hyperuniform (large-scale density fluctuations suppressed) and disordered, filling space evenly without introducing regular patterns. This makes them perceptually favorable, well suited to numerical integration, and effective for aliasing-free sampling. We borrow insights from the study of hyperuniform point sets in condensed matter physics and show that optimizing the disordered ground states of stealthy potentials yields blue noise that saturates the spectral-gap limit. Such point sets can be obtained by plain gradient descent, without early stopping. Using bond-orientational order parameters from the study of 2D melting, we map the Pareto frontier between uniformity and disorder, giving a real-space characterization that complements the standard spectral view of blue noise. We extend the method to non-Euclidean manifolds, combine stealthy losses over unions of point sets to construct multi-class blue noise that enables runtime-adjustable variable-density sampling, and apply reprojective constraints so that such point sets can be stored as textures. Finally, we generalize the loss from suppressing Fourier modes to matching arbitrary spectral targets, and introduce a spatially-varying frequency budget that scales each point's constrained modes by local density, enabling stippling that maintains consistent visual quality at all densities without crystallization artifacts.

10.1145/3842561.title: CADRec: Reconstructing a CAD Sequence Recursively with Localized Geometric Contexts
10.1145/3842561.abstract: We present CADRec, a recursive CAD sequence reconstruction framework based on a hierarchically defined CAD DSL. This method addresses two limitations of previous methods. First, the flat, lengthy script representation of LLM-based reconstruction methods hinders generalization and does not take into account the reuse of code snippets. Second, existing one-shot and iterative geometric context encodings lack the structural clues necessary to accurately localize the geometric context for subsequent sequence reconstruction. CADRec recursively decomposes the input shape into spatially localized parts and reconstructs each part with a local CADQuery program based on a hierarchical CAD DSL. At each node of the hierarchy, the model decides whether to further split the current part into child parts or stop and synthesize its leaf-level CAD script. The generated local programs are then mapped back to the global coordinate frame and composed into the final CAD model. This hierarchical formulation turns global CAD reconstruction into a sequence of simpler local part prediction problems, reducing geometric complexity while preserving the structural organization of the design. To support this process, we encode localized point-cloud context and use an MLLM-based decoder to predict decomposition decisions and CAD programs. We further train the model with geometry-aware objectives that encourage consistent part decomposition and spatially grounded predictions. Experiments on standard CAD reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate that CADRec improves both geometric fidelity and program validity over prior sequence- and code-based baselines. Notably, the robustness of our approach is particularly evident in cross-dataset scenarios: when trained on the limited DeepCAD dataset and tested on the unseen Fusion360 set, our method drastically reduces mean CD, median CD, and IR by 85.8%, 67.2%, and 92.3%, respectively. The code and data for this paper are available on: https://github.com/shinodashx/CADRec.

10.1145/3842566.title: A unified multi-scale method for simulating two-phase immiscible flows
10.1145/3842566.abstract: We present a novel method for simulating large-scale, high density-ratio two-phase immiscible flows. Our approach adopts a two-fluid mixture formulation discretized on a shared Eulerian grid, in which phase fractions are represented using Lagrangian material points. We carefully adapt established closure models to this hybrid framework to capture the exchange of forces between phases, enabling the smooth transition between stratified (grid-resolved) and dispersed (sub-grid) flow regimes without recourse to secondary solvers. The resulting volumetric coupling forces are jointly integrated in a pressure projection, yielding a strongly coupled scheme that remains stable under large time steps and in highly dynamic scenarios. By combining these features, our method provides a unified, multi-scale discretization capable of capturing immiscible two-phase flows covering a large range of spatial scales in a single simulation. We illustrate our method's capabilities on a diverse set of multi-scale scenarios, including a massive waterfall, a waterbombing airplane, large underwater bubbles, a geyser, and crashing ocean waves.

10.1145/3842586.title: IntentGaze: Task-Aligned Gaze Correction for Stable and Responsive Gaze Interaction in XR
10.1145/3842586.abstract: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), China and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong Gaze-contingent XR systems require gaze input that is accurate, responsive, and stable under realistic head, body, and environmental motion. However, raw gaze is affected by fixation jitter, pursuit lag, saccadic transitions, and motion-induced disturbances. Filtering suppresses jitter but often trades responsiveness for stability, while gaze prediction typically estimates future measured samples for latency compensation rather than the task-aligned gaze direction needed for interaction. We formulate online XR gaze correction as causal task-aligned gaze estimation, where intended gaze is treated as the interaction task-defined direction that users are instructed to fixate on or track. To support this formulation, we designed controlled fixation, pursuit, and saccade-related tasks and collected a multi-context gaze dataset from 35 participants, comprising 6.69 million synchronized frames of measured gaze, task-defined target directions, head/body motion signals, and gaze-behavior annotations across sitting, standing, lying down, walking, and simulated vehicle movement. Based on this dataset, we introduce IntentGaze, a motion-FiLM residual correction model that predicts current-frame task-aligned gaze corrections from recent gaze and motion histories. The model uses gaze dynamics for residual correction, motion features for contextual modulation, and saccade-aware control to preserve rapid gaze transitions. In subject-independent evaluation, IntentGaze achieved mean angular errors of 0.57° for fixation and 1.30° for pursuit, reducing errors by 29% and 18% compared with the strongest baseline. It also reduced gaze instability to 0.21° and 0.88°, corresponding to reductions of 33% and 9%. Additional analyses show that motion-conditioned modulation mainly benefits motion-rich conditions, saccade-aware control reduces transition lag to approximately one frame, reduced-sensor cross-device evaluation preserves performance on another XR headset, and replay-based dwell selection indicates potential target-acquisition benefits. The compact model further supports online deployment without dedicated acceleration in runtime XR systems. These results suggest that causal task-aligned gaze estimation can serve as a practical runtime correction layer for stable and responsive gaze interaction in XR.

10.1145/3842589.title: Tight Quad-Dominant Tri-Quad Cage Construction for 3D Shapes
10.1145/3842589.abstract: Cages are compact geometric proxies widely used in computer graphics. Existing cage generation methods mainly focus on triangular cages. In this paper, we present the first automatic method for constructing high-quality quad-dominant tri-quad cages. Generating such cages is challenging because topology editing, geometric approximation, validity, and quadrilateral dominance are highly coupled in a constrained optimization problem. We make the problem tractable by decoupling topology and geometry while maintaining all cage-validity requirements throughout the pipeline, including being self-intersection-free, collision-free and feature-preserving. Starting from a feasible quad-dominant offset surface extracted from the signed distance field (SDF) of the input, we first perform constrained simplification. In this process, metric-aware and direction-preserving topology edits reduce complexity and suppress unnecessary triangles only when validity checks are satisfied. We then optimize the simplified feasible cage under the same validity constraints by minimizing a fidelity-and-quality energy that encourages tight approximation, rectangularity, smoothness, and orientation coherence. Because every update remains feasible and decreases the objective, validity is preserved by construction, and the algorithm converges to a stable local optimum. Comparative experiments demonstrate that our method produces tight, collision-free, and self-intersection-free quad-dominant tri-quad cages with high geometric fidelity and coherent directional structure. We further demonstrate their utility in nested cages construction, simplification, cage-based deformation, and subdivision-surface generation, showing advantages in approximation quality, deformation control, and directional coherence.

10.1145/3842542.title: Event-Based Shape and Reflectance Acquisition Using the Refresh Line of a Single Off-the-Shelf Display
10.1145/3842542.abstract: Capturing the shape and spatially varying reflectance of objects is fundamental to many graphics and vision applications, yet achieving fast acquisition remains challenging. Existing display-based appearance capture methods rely on a sequence of multiple illumination patterns and measurements to disentangle illumination, geometry, material response, and sensor characteristics. However, pattern switching and multi-frame capture are time-consuming, limiting acquisition speed and applicability to dynamic scenarios. In this paper, we observe that the native row-wise refresh lines of commodity displays already provide a fast spatiotemporal illumination signal within a single frame. Combining this with a high-temporal-resolution event camera, we capture object appearance changes within one frame during the display's progressive scanning. Based on this signal, we propose a method to simultaneously reconstruct shape and reflectance from the event stream induced by refresh lines. We build a prototype system that pairs a commodity OLED display with an event camera to capture refresh-line responses from near-planar, highly metallic objects. Using this setup, we develop a reconstruction pipeline that uses event measurements to recover surface shape and spatially varying reflectance. Through 25 fps real-time capture and offline reconstruction on real near-planar metallic objects, we demonstrate that native display refresh can be repurposed from an imaging artifact into a practical high-speed cue for appearance acquisition.

10.1145/3842569.title: Learned pi metalens for wide-field-of-view near-infrared imaging
10.1145/3842569.abstract: Wide—field-of-view (FoV) near-infrared (NIR) imaging is vital for compact augmented reality and robotic systems. Conventional wide-FoV optics rely on bulky compound refractive optics, limiting miniaturization. Metalenses composed of sub-wavelength meta-atoms offer a compact alternative. However, achieving high transmission and complete 2 π phase coverage simultaneously over wide angle-of-incidence (AOI) remains challenging, leading to blur and non-uniform efficiency across the field. Here, we present a learned π metalens based on an AOI-aware design framework that achieves uniform-quality 100° FoV NIR imaging. Rather than enforcing full 2 π phase control, we leverage meta-atoms that maintain high-transmission across wide angular ranges, which inherently exhibit restricted phase coverage. To design such a phase-limited metalens, we introduce a differentiable phase-limited metalens representation that incorporates the AOI-aware vectorial response of meta-atoms. This effectively learns a metalens using phase-limited high-transmission meta-atoms, yielding improvements in focusing efficiency and image sharpness across a wide FoV. Our learned π metalens demonstrates a 14% improvement in modulation transfer function at the largest AOI and a 2.4x enhancement in focusing-efficiency uniformity compared to conventional quadratic 2 π metalenses. Our results suggest that, when AOI-dependent responses are properly modeled, complete 2 π phase coverage is not strictly required for high-performance wide-FoV metalenses, opening new opportunities for compact NIR imaging systems in robotics, human-computer interaction, and eye-tracking in extended reality systems.

10.1145/3842543.title: PhotoMaster: Learning Holistic Capture-Time Decisions for Guided Photography Reshooting
10.1145/3842543.abstract: Capturing compelling photographs requires sequential capture-time decisions. However, existing guidance methods operate at the image level rather than modeling the decision process that diagnoses photographic dimensions (e.g., camera position, lighting) and resolves them into executable reshooting actions, offering limited actionable support for novices. We present PhotoMaster, a decision-driven multimodal framework for capture-time photography guidance. To model the decision-making process, we propose the Photography Decision Taxonomy (PDT) that defines photographic dimensions for diagnosing novice-captured photos and maps them to executable actions. To make this intuitive, PhotoMaster pairs these executable actions with a rendered visual target that previews the expected outcome. To learn this decision space, we introduce a two-fold data engine: Forward Decision Transfer distills professional photographers' decisions from masterworks to casual shots, while Decision Inversion applies inverse capture decisions via camera-controllable world models, collectively yielding over 230K PDT-annotated triplets. Evaluations demonstrate PhotoMaster's capability to produce expert-aligned diagnoses and highly preferred visual references, while a real-world user study confirms that novices achieve significantly better captures using our framework.

10.1145/3842560.title: Field Optimization for Scalable and Distortion-Aware Process Planning in Hybrid Additive-Subtractive Manufacturing
10.1145/3842560.abstract: This paper presents a field-based optimization method for process planning in hybrid manufacturing, where the goal is to determine a feasible and efficient sequence of additive and subtractive operations for fabricating a target shape. Existing approaches rely on deterministic or discretized formulations, which lead to unoptimized fabrication time and make planning sensitive to voxel resolution. They also do not explicitly account for distortion in intermediate structures formed during manufacturing. To address these limitations, we represent manufacturing states using continuous fields, which scale naturally to models with large dimensions and fine geometric features while enabling smoother fabrication sequences. Based on this representation, we formulate process planning as a numerical optimization problem under multiple objectives, including final shape conformance, intermediate structural strength, manufacturing time, self-supporting, and collision avoidance. Experimental results show that our method can generate distortion-aware process plans on a variety of models while substantially reducing fabrication time through up to a 72.6% reduction in the volume of extra support.

10.1145/3842587.title: AnyStitch: Generative Large Parallax Image Stitching
10.1145/3842587.abstract: Wide field-of-view panorama stitching is important for computational photography and immersive visual applications, but often faces some challenges like severe geometric disparities. The typical "warp-and-blend" stitching technique only works with limited parallax and fails on large-parallax scenes, due to its inherent restriction to 2D geometric transformations that cannot resolve underlying 3D structures. To break this limitation, we present AnyStitch, a generative framework that can merge multiple reference images with large parallax into a seamless panorama. Unlike previous methods, we formulate the stitching problem as a reference-based image generation process, which naturally avoids stitching artifacts. Specifically, we propose a Hierarchical Projected Rotary Positional Encoding (HPRoPE) based on a 3D feed-forward model to establish accurate geometric relationships between the inputs and the panoramic canvas while preserving fidelity. Given that the resolution of the generated image varies with the number of inputs, we design a spatial autoregressive generation strategy to generate visually coherent panoramas at flexible resolutions. Finally, to enable the supervised fine-tuning of the proposed model, we construct a paired dataset utilizing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scenes. Experiments demonstrate that AnyStitch can seamlessly stitch a variable number of inputs (like 22 views in teaser) with large camera motion, support flexible control of target view and projection type, and handle simple dynamic scenes. Project page: https://cecret3350.github.io/AnyStitch/.

10.1145/3842565.title: SDR-ToF: Million Optical Depth Samples per Second Using Software-Defined Radio
10.1145/3842565.abstract: We present a continuous-wave time-of-flight (CW-ToF) sensing system capable of megahertz-rate depth measurements using a free-space laser and commodity radio-frequency (RF) communication hardware. Existing highspeed optical displacement and vibration sensing systems typically rely on optical interferometry or specialized heterodyne electronics, making them complex and expensive to deploy. We instead show that commodity software-defined radios (SDRs) can serve as a programmable optical sensing backend by jointly performing laser modulation and RF demodulation of signals measured by a fast photodiode. This architecture enables direct phase-based depth estimation at megahertz temporal rates without requiring optical interferometry. Because both the modulation frequency and readout pipeline are fully programmable in software, the system allows flexible trade-offs between depth range, precision, and temporal bandwidth. The resulting sensor supports high-speed depth and vibration measurements, enabling applications such as monitoring rapidly moving mechanical systems, and reconstructing acoustic signals from vibrating surfaces. We experimentally evaluate a prototype system across multiple sensing scenarios and demonstrate submillimeter depth sensitivity at megahertz sampling rates, while analyzing practical limitations including noise, drift, and hardware constraints. Our results show that commodity RF hardware can enable low-cost, high-speed optical depth sensing , opening new opportunities for computational imaging and dynamic scene analysis.

10.1145/3842551.title: TORO Curves: G^2 Interpolating Curve with Maximum Curvature Control
10.1145/3842551.abstract: We introduce TORO curves, a new family of G 2 -continuous interpolating splines that provide precise local curvature control without global optimization. Our construction assembles two types of primitive segments, each attaining curvature maxima strictly on the endpoint circular arcs: the trigonometric offset (TO) segment for inflection transitions, and the rational Bézier offset (RO) segment for constant-sign curvature spans. A core pillar of our framework is an offset-based decoupling strategy: by exploiting properties of offset curves, we decouple the geometry from the curvature magnitude, thereby enabling direct curvature prescription at control points. The construction is deterministic and local; each segment is solved via simple quadratic equations, and the rational Bézier weights are directly determined by geometric quantities. This provides strict local support and enables realtime responsiveness during interactive manipulation. Finally, we introduce an adaptive curvature configuration that guarantees robustness and visual continuity under deformation. Our results demonstrate that TORO curves can represent complex shapes while accurately reproducing basic primitives such as circular arcs and ellipses, offering an efficient, versatile tool for modern geometric design.

10.1145/3842556.title: Stitch Graphs for Interactive Modeling of Non-Local Knit Topologies
10.1145/3842556.abstract: Knitwear design requires precise, stitch-level editing, as individual loops dictate both the fabric's texture and its final 3D shape. While stitch meshes have enabled interactive modeling by representing knits as polygonal surfaces, many complex knitted structures feature intricate yarn paths that depart from a surface-like topology. To address this, we propose stitch graphs. By representing knitting operations as nodes in a graph, we leverage non-local connectivity to naturally model crossings and long-range connections. Our complete framework for modeling, simulation, and yarn visualization with stitch graphs enables real-time, interactive design of complex structures including volumetric cables, stacked tucks, and dimensional ribbing. We further introduce a unified editing tool that handles transfers, cables, and tucks through a single interaction model. We validate our method against representative patterns and physical samples, demonstrating that stitch graphs provide a robust and versatile foundation for interactive, swatch-level knit design.

10.1145/3842536.title: Efficient and Robust Seamless Parametrization
10.1145/3842536.abstract: Seamless surface parametrizations support many important geometry processing tasks, including quad meshing, texture mapping, and patch-based surface representations. Recent intrinsic approaches based on Penner coordinates provide a robust mechanism for constructing feasible, seamless parametrizations with prescribed topological structure, determined by a guiding field on a surface and detected feature lines, overcoming many robustness limitations of previous methods. However, these methods rely on highly accurate nonlinear solves, which present a significant obstacle to scalability on large, densely sampled meshes. We address this challenge by observing that Penner-coordinate methods are primarily needed to establish an initial feasible solution whose structure depends on overall guiding field topology and surface topology rather than fine geometric detail, and that high-precision optimization is unnecessary for achieving high-quality results at full resolution, as long as the coarse initial solution can be transferred to the fine levels, while maintaining constraints. We propose a three-scale pipeline that combines an efficient hierarchical approach with robust Penner-coordinate methods. Our method computes guiding fields and holonomy on a medium-resolution mesh, solves the Penner-coordinate feasibility problem efficiently on a coarse mesh that permits connectivity changes, and transfers the resulting structure to the original fine mesh, where only a final, scalable optimization and quantization are performed. Experiments on large benchmark and real-world models demonstrate substantial speedups with no change in robustness in the processing of meshes with millions of triangles.

10.1145/3842557.title: SwiftFusion: Towards Motion-Robust and Efficient 4K HDR Fusion
10.1145/3842557.abstract: High Dynamic Range (HDR) imaging remains a fundamental challenge in camera system design. Although recent diffusion-based methods have achieved promising visual quality for HDR fusion, they still suffer from significant limitations in robustness to dynamic scenes and prohibitively slow inference speeds, which make them difficult to apply to high-resolution HDR fusion in practice. To address these issues, we propose SwiftFusion , an efficient generative framework designed for high-resolution HDR fusion in complex dynamic scenes. It decomposes 4K HDR fusion into a motion-aware low-resolution fusion module with video priors, and a high-frequency-guided decoding module for faithful 4K reconstruction. Specifically, first, we propose a Motion-Robust Fusion Module, which remodels dynamic HDR fusion as an exposure-conditioned pseudo-video generation problem. This module uses a tailored condition-injection design to adapt pretrained video model for robust large-motion deghosting. Second, we design a High-Frequency Guided Decoder that extracts structural details from 4K LDR inputs and incorporates them into the decoding process as guidance. With a lightweight multi-scale design, this module can efficiently reconstruct low-resolution latents to 4K HDR images. Third, to further accelerate inference, we develop an acceleration pipeline that introduces a Condition-Aware Sparse Attention mechanism to reduce attention overhead and distills the flow-matching backbone into a one-step generator for accelerated sampling. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SwiftFusion achieves excellent deghosting capability and structural fidelity in highly challenging dynamic scenarios. Notably, SwiftFusion generates a 4K HDR image in only 2.2 seconds , achieving an impressive 198 × inference speedup compared with existing generative HDR approaches. Code is available at https://openimaginglab.github.io/SwiftFusion/

10.1145/3842564.title: Dynamic GPU Voxel Grids and Voxel-sequential Processing in NanoVDB
10.1145/3842564.abstract: We introduce two fundamental advances to the NanoVDB data structure: dynamic GPU-native topological updates, and a voxel-sequential access paradigm that dramatically accelerates point-wise and stencil-based operators on sparse grids. NanoVDB's linearized memory layout has delivered strong GPU performance, and the Index-Grid concept introduced in the fVDB framework [Williams et al. 2024] provided topology/data separation and optimal compactness of storage in sparse machine learning workloads. However, all these prior iterations of NanoVDB assume a static topology that has precluded use of this data structure in simulation and dynamic geometric processes. We eliminate this limitation by introducing a suite of dynamic topology operators - morphological dilation, grid merging, pruning, and cross-resolution coarsening and refinement. These operators use bit-parallel algorithms to reconstruct grids containing hundreds of millions of voxels in just a few milliseconds. We also introduce a voxel-sequential access paradigm and data structure for GPU kernels operating on sparse data. We stream active voxels as a flat linear sequence, minimizing or eliminating the need for tree traversal in the process. This achieves compute density and regularity that allow even complex stencil-based operators to approach peak memory bandwidth, with minimal storage overhead. Together, these contributions remove the read-only constraint from NanoVDB, establishing it as a high-performance primary representation for dynamic GPU simulation and geometry manipulation. We evaluate the efficacy of our newly introduced operators in benchmarks sourced from applications such as 3D reconstruction, fluid simulation, and large-scale mesh voxelization.

10.1145/3842538.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
10.1145/3842538.abstract: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.

10.1145/3842539.title: AROMA : Augmented Reality Optimized Tone Mapping
10.1145/3842539.abstract: AROMA is a tone mapping operator designed to optimize the visual fidelity of images displayed on optical see-through augmented reality (AR) devices, which are often challenged by limited dynamic range and substantial ambient light interference. The system aims to faithfully preserve the perceived color, brightness, and contrast of source images with moderate dynamic range, even when the display's effective dynamic range is significantly lower than that of the content. Rather than enhancing or altering the original appearance, AROMA aims to maintain perceptual equivalence, replicating original intent as closely as possible on the target display. To achieve this, AROMA employs a global tone curve minimizing perceived contrast distortion, complemented by adaptive detail enhancement to selectively restore high-frequency details lost due to dynamic range compression, and color saturation correction. AROMA 's approach to dynamic range mapping accounts for ambient light by adjusting the tone curve to maximize the display's usable range, ensuring that the final image is both perceptually accurate and visually pleasing, even in challenging lighting environments. A subjective study was conducted, demonstrating that AROMA significantly improves perceived visual quality, achieving results equivalent to a 45–59% increase in display luminance. As a result, AROMA can be used to enable AR rendering at lower display power, producing substantial energy savings without compromising user experience. Finally, AROMA is lightweight and feasible within form-factor-constrained head-mounted AR displays — our implementation runs at 250 FPS on Meta Ray-Ban Display AR glasses. 1

10.1145/3842524.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
10.1145/3842524.abstract: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. This paradigm carries two intrinsic limitations. First, VAE reconstruction removes fine geometric detail before the diffusion model ever sees the data. Second, the two-stage pipeline creates an objective mismatch, since the VAE is trained for reconstruction whereas the diffusion model is trained for distribution matching. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF grids into meshes via Marching Cubes so that rendered normal losses can supervise the model directly from its predicted SDF. To improve alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry, Direct3D-V3 also predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image as an auxiliary task, encouraging the DiT to learn the mapping from image observations to 3D shape. This latent-free design removes the reconstruction bottleneck, brings training under an objective in the native voxel domain, and yields meshes with substantially richer local detail. The predicted camera and native SDF voxel output further make Direct3D-V3 extensible to generative reconstruction, where diffusion is interleaved with normal-guided refinement to improve alignment with the observed view while the generative prior completes unseen regions. Extensive experiments show that Direct3D-V3 achieves competitive results to state-of-the-art latent-based methods, while producing finer geometry.

10.1145/3842537.title: Hypergraph Rotation Systems: A Unified Framework for Linked Knot Structures
10.1145/3842537.abstract: We present a unified framework for the design of linked knot (LK) structures including links, knots, weaves, knits, and chainmail structures, extending them to articulated and compliant (spring-like) assemblies. The core of our approach is a combinatorial representation based on Hypergraph Rotation Systems (H-GRS) , in which topology is defined by the cyclic ordering of incidences between faces and edges. This formulation removes the need for manifold assumptions or global orientation, naturally supporting non-manifold connectivity. Building on this representation, we introduce integer-valued twist assignments on edges as local operators that deterministically control global cycle structure, linking, and connectivity. These operators enable the systematic construction of both unicursal (single-cycle) and multi-component configurations, which can exhibit different forms of compliant and articulated behavior. Unlike prior approaches based on manifold constraints or binary twisting, our framework supports multi-valued twisting and higher-order connectivity, enabling selective linking, partial merging, and articulated couplings not achievable in classical textile constructions. We demonstrate the framework across a wide range of structures and validate it through physical prototypes fabricated via 3D printing and paper-strip construction on a scaffold. By unifying combinatorial topology with the exploration of mechanical behavior, H-GRS provides a minimal and extensible foundation for the topology-driven design of linked filament structures, with applications in computational fabrication, architectured materials, and bio-inspired systems.

10.1145/3842555.title: TiCHPolyU: Polygonal Urban Reconstruction via Tight Convex Hull
10.1145/3842555.abstract: With the development of digital urban environments, establishing lightweight models for architectural ensembles has gained significant importance. We propose TiCHPolyU , a polygonal mesh reconstruction method to address this need. The core idea of TiCHPolyU is to construct a tight convex hull from raw architectural input, forming a 2.5 D structure generated from the ground that represents the basic geometry of the model. Building on this structure, TiCHPolyU performs a spatial partition to reconstruct geometric details while preserving manifold compactness. The method produces polygonal meshes with improved geometric consistency and reduced data volume. Compared to traditional solutions, TiCHPolyU provides greater efficiency and practicality without requiring additional feature support.

10.1145/3842581.title: MeRM: Large Mesh Reconstruction Model via Neural Geometry Tokens
10.1145/3842581.abstract: High-fidelity surface reconstruction from sparse RGB images remains a significant challenge, where classical optimization-based approaches typically fail to resolve geometric ambiguity under insufficient epipolar constraints. While recent feed-forward methods have achieved remarkable progress in directly regressing point clouds and 3D Gaussians from sparse inputs, extending such paradigms to explicit surface reconstruction often results in suboptimal geometric quality. We identify the primary obstacle in feed-forward surface reconstruction as an inherent structural misalignment between 2D visual inputs and 3D surface targets, which creates a learning bottleneck and leads to degraded performance. In this work, we propose MeRM, a large-scale feed-forward Mesh Reconstruction Model that leverages a novel Neural Geometry Token (NGT) technique to address this challenge. Our key insight is that intermediate tokens of a multi-view Transformer—pretrained to predict dense depth maps, normal maps, and masks—can serve as a powerful geometric pre-aggregator to bridge the structural bottleneck. Benefiting from the highly informative geometric cues distilled by NGT, our MeRM delivers exceptional surface reconstruction quality while maintaining impressive training and inference efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our MeRM significantly outperforms prior feed-forward methods and even exceeds the performance of state-of-the-art optimization-based approaches on dense views, despite using only sparse inputs. We believe our approach establishes a novel framework for large-scale feed-forward mesh reconstruction, paving a new path for future research.

10.1145/3842554.title: RAWVAR: Visual Autoregressive Modeling for Color-Faithful Low-Light RAW Image Restoration
10.1145/3842554.abstract: Visual autoregressive (VAR) modeling provides a promising generative solution for RGB image restoration, owing to its strong ability to generate realistic details and recover rich scene information. Nevertheless, directly applying VAR to low-light RAW image restoration still presents two main challenges. First, RGB-pretrained VAE tokenizers are mismatched with RAW sensor statistics, causing color bias after domain transfer. Second, VAR requires tiled inference for high-resolution RAW images, where independent token prediction across tiles may introduce color discrepancies that are further amplified by the Image Signal Processing (ISP) pipeline. To address these issues, we propose RAWVAR, the first visual autoregressive framework for low-light RAW image restoration. For effective domain transfer, we design a Cross-Domain Codebook (CDC), which freezes the RGB-pretrained encoder and original codebook while appending a trainable RAW-domain codebook, forming a cross-domain latent space for texture-preserving and color-faithful RAW representation. To mitigate color inconsistency during tiled inference, we further design a Position-aware Token Alignment (PTA) strategy. During coarse-to-fine prediction, PTA aligns the token logits of semantically corresponding regions across tiles, ensuring consistent predictions for shared content. Furthermore, a Global Color Refinement (GCR) module globally refines the discrete latents to enhance image-wise color consistency. Compared with diffusion-based methods, RAWVAR provides a more efficient generative restoration pipeline by avoiding iterative denoising. Extensive experiments show that RAWVAR produces color-faithful and perceptually superior results, outperforming existing generative restoration methods.

10.1145/3842588.title: High-fidelity Multi-view Hair Reconstruction via Spherical Orientation Distribution Functions
10.1145/3842588.abstract: High-fidelity multi-view 3D hair reconstruction from casual handheld captures remains a formidable challenge due to severe self-occlusions and the intricate topology of individual strands. A critical bottleneck in existing 3D hair representations—both volumetric grids and continuous implicit fields—is the reliance on deterministic spatial queries that assign a single local orientation. This unimodal assumption inevitably collapses and averages crossing or layered strands into erroneous directions, leading to a loss of internal structural details. To overcome this, we introduce SODF-Hair, a novel framework that represents local hair structures using Spherical Orientation Distribution Functions (SODFs). By encoding a multi-modal distribution within each voxel, our SODF representation effectively resolves the structural ambiguities of tangled and overlapping fibers, preserving complex local variations even under limited grid resolutions. Our pipeline explicitly decomposes the reconstruction into exterior observation and interior completion. To bridge 2D image evidence into 3D, we first reconstruct a visible hair-segment shell using fixed-scale oriented 3D Gaussian proxies. Their elongated covariances yield projections that match the streak-like texture of visible hair in the input images, enabling the recovery of fine visible segment geometry while preventing the proxies from degenerating into free-form blobs. We then formulate the recovery of invisible internal structures as an inpainting task. A geometry-conditioned probabilistic model, leveraging a compact latent SODF codec and rectified flow matching, predicts the missing multi-modal distributions within the closed volume. Finally, rather than prematurely committing to a single streamline, we assemble explicit scalp-connected strands via a field-guided beam search and constrained graph optimization. Extensive evaluations suggest that our approach faithfully preserves subject-specific visible details while generating structurally coherent internal strand geometry, demonstrating robust performance across diverse hairstyles.

10.1145/3842541.title: Lanczos Advection: Near-Orthogonal Semi-Lagrangian Reconstruction for Fluid Simulation
10.1145/3842541.abstract: Producing vivid fluid details, such as the sharp spatial structure of interfaces and vortices, is essential for high-quality fluid simulations in computer graphics. The advection solver is a vital component of fluid simulation, and the semi-Lagrangian method is widely adopted as a central building block for many advanced advection methods thanks to its unconditional stability. Despite these notable improvements, the numerical dissipation and energy loss inherent in conventional linear interpolation remain considerable drawbacks, compromising visual fidelity. This paper proposes a novel extension of the core semi-Lagrangian advection algorithm to significantly alleviate numerical dissipation and energy loss. Our extension uses a dimension-splitting weighted sum with a windowed sinc (also known as Lanczos) kernel, leveraging the properties of the sinc function to construct a bounded, near-orthogonal semi-Lagrangian reconstruction. Our experiments, comparing various advection methods and their discrete operators, demonstrate that our extension significantly improves the orthogonality of the operator, energy-retaining behavior and enables richer visual details.

10.1145/3842573.title: Robust Deformation-based 3D Bijective Mapping through Differential Boundary Shape Matching
10.1145/3842573.abstract: We introduce a novel framework to generate piecewise linear tetrahedral maps, by expressing the map-finding problem as a constrained mesh deformation problem, where constraints satisfaction implies both injectivity and target shape conformity. Deformation is supported by the two core components of our approach: First, an augmentation of the mesh by boundary-incident virtual elements, encoding the target shape in a differential manner via its first and second fundamental form; in contrast to position-driven approaches this prevents optimisation failure due to improper winding. Second, a remeshing scheme maintaining mesh element quality and preventing blocking configurations. A first implementation is empirically shown to have higher robustness and/or higher efficiency than state-of-the-art methods on challenging, yet practically relevant inputs. We illustrate our method's versatility in a range of applications, demonstrating its value as a new item in the algorithmic toolbox for volumetric mapping.

10.1145/3842575.title: Capturing Rich Details of Human Eyes
10.1145/3842575.abstract: Capturing rich details of human eyes is essential for realistic digital humans, yet remains challenging due to the eye's complex optical structure. The sclera, cornea, and iris exhibit distinct appearance properties, and their geometry and appearance are tightly coupled through reflection and refraction in image observations. We present a human eye capture and reconstruction system based on multi-source optical measurements, which are tailored to different eye components to capture detail-rich observations at multiple scales and provide direct constraints for staged, decoupled reconstruction. For the sclera, multi-view and multi-gaze imaging recovers subject-specific exterior geometry and establishes an eye-centric frame. For the cornea, specular highlights and dense Placido-based topographic cues estimate the anterior surface before it is used as the refractive interface for iris reconstruction. For the iris, refraction-aware photometric reconstruction recovers albedo, normals, and fine-scale displacement under limited viewing angles. Experiments demonstrate detailed reconstruction of scleral shape, corneal topography, and iris micro-geometry across diverse subjects. The reconstructed assets further expose physiology-supported ocular details, including scleral asymmetry, non-axisymmetric corneal shape, iris relief, and pupil-center motion, providing evidence for reconstruction fidelity and useful annotations for downstream rendering, tracking, and data generation. We will release a consented 20-eye reconstructed ocular asset dataset containing component models and textures for all eye components.

10.1145/3842570.title: Ortho-arc Curves: Generative Design of Developable Bands and Polygonal Tubes
10.1145/3842570.abstract: The design of developable surfaces from closed directrices with prescribed symmetry and non-trivial topology is usually treated through iterative optimization. We introduce ortho-arc curves (OACs), C 1 piecewise-circular curves generated from polygonal paths on a support surface, as part of a forward analytic approach distinct from inverse shape approximation. For closed OACs, we show that rotation-minimizing-frame closure is governed by quantized signed accumulated torsion, and use this criterion to generate one-parameter families of patchwise exactly developable bands. The resulting bands are assembled from planar, cylindrical, and conical patches joined with C 1 continuity globally. With compatible polygonal cross-sections, we further construct polygonal tubes with developable faces. Through polyhedral precursors, we control the geometry and topology of the OAC directrices by construction, and from spherical duality and indicatrix deformations we obtain continuous families with fixed orientability type. Beyond the core construction, we prove that the ortho-arc condition and rotation-minimizing frame holonomy are preserved under Möbius transformations in R 3 , with chirality reversal under orientation-reversing maps. Finally, we illustrate knotted and linked topologies and outline exploratory extensions to reciprocal-frame-like cylinder scaffolds, piecewise-helical directrices, and higher-regularity directrices retaining the properties of precursor-driven topology and frame-holonomy control. These results provide a generative route to developable band and polygonal tube design for fabrication-oriented workflows.

10.1145/3842568.title: Quad-mesh based isogonal nets and computational design
10.1145/3842568.abstract: We propose a quad-mesh-based framework for discrete isogonal nets using checkerboard patterns with inscribed parallelograms derived from quad meshes. By controlling the angles, similarity, or congruence of these parallelograms, we obtain three classes of isogonal nets on diagonal or control meshes. These nets admit simple explicit representations, enable diverse shape exploration related to conformal mappings with preserved pattern shapes, and are formulated using explicit, at-most-quadratic constraints for numerical computation and optimization. The third class serves as a discrete model of developable surfaces, grounded in our analysis of smooth isogonal Chebyshev nets and verified through discrete differential geometric quantities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the three proposed nets through pattern designs for shell structures and interactive paper-cutting models, both fabricated with repetitive similar elements.

10.1145/3842533.title: Z++: Temporal, Non-Uniform, and 3D Z Sampling
10.1145/3842533.abstract: Z sampling redistributes Monte Carlo error in screen space by assigning consecutive low-discrepancy sub-sequences to Z-ordered pixels, using differently shuffled 1D or 2D sequences for the individual constituent domains of a light-transport path. We first analyze the reasons that Z sampling is effective and distill a set of practical design guidelines for Z sampling algorithms. We then propose extensions to Z sampling in two complementary directions: temporally across frames, and spatially to non-uniform and higher-dimensional constituent domains. Our approach thus improves temporal frame accumulation by assigning negatively correlated samples to consecutive frames, without additional memory or runtime cost, while preserving individual-frame quality. It further allows applying Z sampling to non-uniform, importance-sampled distributions, via a tabulated hierarchical equal-mass subdivision of the importance map. For 3D constituent integration domains, we also introduce a novel low-discrepancy sequence that simultaneously maintains high uniformity in the full 3D domain, along each coordinate axis, and across each pairwise 2D projection. The proposed sequence is quaternary (base-4) structured, hence optimal stratification is attained only for power-of-four sample counts. We empirically demonstrate the advantage of our approach over the common practice of splitting a 3D constituent domain into a 1D–2D pair, and evaluate it against existing 3D sampling alternatives.

10.1145/3842520.title: Computing a Metric on the Shape Space of Tori
10.1145/3842520.abstract: This paper explores shape comparison for genus-one surfaces, namely tori, through an intrinsic metric on their shape space. While metric structures for 2-spheres are well established, extending them to tori is substantially harder, due to their nontrivial topology and the absence of conformal diffeomorphisms in general. Drawing on Teichmüller theory, we formulate an algorithm that minimizes a distortion energy over diffeomorphisms within a canonical homotopy class to compute a metric on the shape space of Riemannian tori. This produces both a pairwise distance and an optimal, landmark-free correspondence. On the computational side, we discretize this energy on triangulated tori and optimize it directly in a pair of fundamental domains. A key theoretical contribution is a convergence theorem showing that the discrete energy converges to the smooth metric energy under mesh refinement. Experiments on flat tori, tori of revolution, and real-world scanned surfaces show that the method captures natural geometric variation and provides a robust tool for genus-one shape comparison.

10.1145/3842563.title: Metalog Materials
10.1145/3842563.abstract: A central aspect of modern physically based rendering is the practical yet realistic modeling of material appearance, which requires efficient and accurate representations of bidirectional reflectance distribution functions (BRDFs). In this paper, we present a unified material reflectance representation based on metalog distributions. Introducing quantile-based metalog interpolation and metalog mixture models, our representation captures a wide range of complex reflectance behaviors of both analytic models and real-world materials, while remaining interpretable and efficient. Our approach achieves competitive runtime performance and a small memory footprint, while enabling continuous interpolation between fundamentally different reflectance behaviors. Furthermore, our model is fully differentiable with respect to the coefficients defining the distributions, thus easily integrates into existing differentiable rendering pipelines. In summary, metalog materials can effectively represent real-world reflectance data, interpolate between multiple materials within a unified representation, and be acquired from real-world images via differentiable rendering.

10.1145/3842535.title: Beyond Kirchhoff-Love: A Volumetric Approach to Thin-Shell Mechanics
10.1145/3842535.abstract: We present a thin-shell energy formulation rigorously derived from first volumetric principles of 3D solid mechanics, overcoming limitations of prior methods that rely on geometric heuristics or restrictive assumptions such as those in Kirchhoff-Love shells. Our approach supports arbitrary nonlinear isotropic materials, reproduces volumetric behavior exactly under small deformations, and remains accurate for large deformations. Kirchhoff-Love thin shells constrain material lines normal to the mid-surface to remain straight, normal, and unstretched, suppressing through-thickness relaxation. As a result, they fail to reproduce the behavior of the corresponding 3D volumetric material such as Poisson contraction or bending-induced through-thickness nonlinearities, even under small deformations. We analytically derive the leading small-deformation through-thickness modes of an initially flat thin shell from volumetric elasticity: a linear normal mode that scales the local thickness, a quadratic normal mode that captures bending-induced thickness variation, and higher modes. We use the lowest modes as a compact kinematic ansatz for large-deformation thin-shell simulation, with a scalar thickness variable ρ and an optional, statically condensable bending amplitude ζ. Starting from an arbitrary isotropic hyperelastic energy density ψ , we derive a closed-form shell energy by expanding the deformation gradient through the thickness and analytically integrating the volumetric energy. The resulting energy separates stretching and bending contributions, avoids both volumetric meshing and through-thickness quadrature, and depends only on mid-surface quantities (the first fundamental form and the shape operator), together with ρ and ζ. We provide robust implementation-ready formulas for the energy, gradient, and Hessian, including systematic treatment of removable singularities that arise when principal stretches coincide. Experiments show close agreement with volumetric simulations across diverse materials and scenarios, greatly surpassing KL shells, while retaining the computational efficiency of thin shells.

10.1145/502122.502124.title: Spherical averages and applications to spherical splines and interpolation
10.1145/502122.502124.abstract: This article introduces a method for computing weighted averages on spheres based on least squares minimization that respects spherical distance. We prove existence and uniqueness properties of the weighted averages, and give fast iterative algorithms with linear and quadratic convergence rates. Our methods are appropriate to problems involving averages of spherical data in meteorological, geophysical, and astronomical applications. One simple application is a method for smooth averaging of quaternions, which generalizes Shoemake's spherical linear interpolation.The weighted averages methods allow a novel method of defining Bézier and spline curves on spheres, which provides direct generalization of Bézier and B-spline curves to spherical spline curves. We present a fast algorithm for spline interpolation on spheres.
